intro_band.agent_remit_summary: An autonomous agent built on the Fetch.ai uAgents framework, holding a cryptographic identity and an on-chain wallet, that performs operator-defined tasks on a schedule and in response to inbound messages from other agents. It is authorized to send, receive and broadcast structured messages, register and refresh its own record on the Almanac and Agentverse, resolve peer addresses, read and write its own key-value store, and sign with its identity — and nothing more. Its counterparties are a closed, operator-configured set of peer agents, and its channels are its own inbound endpoint, the Agentverse mailbox or proxy, the Almanac registry and the ledger. Host shell access is forbidden outright, on-chain value transfers are out of scope unless the operator explicitly authorizes them, and the agent-inspector and other debug REST endpoints must be disabled in production.
intro_band.agent_structure_summary: A Python framework runtime in two packages — uagents (agent lifecycle, ASGI server, dispatch, registration, resolver, storage) and uagents-core (identity, envelope, protocol, logging). Agent in agent.py owns an ECDSA secp256k1 identity and a cosmpy LocalWallet, registers on the Almanac contract or Agentverse at startup, and serves inbound envelopes through ASGIServer in asgi.py, which binds 0.0.0.0 with wildcard CORS and forwarded_allow_ips="*". Inbound envelopes are signature-verified and schema-validated before dispatcher.dispatch_msg() routes them to typed handlers; there is no shell, subprocess, eval or deserialization surface anywhere in the runtime. Beyond the remit's shape, the runtime enables four agent-inspector REST routes by default, ships no counterparty allowlist on the default message path, and persists identity and wallet private keys as plaintext JSON in the working directory.

behavior_summary: The dominant pattern is a runtime that authenticates its peers but never authorizes them. Envelope signatures are genuinely verified with ECDSA in asgi.py and envelope.py, yet nothing downstream asks whether a verified sender is an authorized counterparty: the AccessControlList that would answer that question lives in the opt-in QuotaProtocol and defaults to allow-all, and the signed envelope carries expires and nonce fields that the receive path never checks, so a captured message replays forever. Compounding this, the agent-inspector REST routes are on by default behind a loopback check that forwarded_allow_ips="*" makes spoofable on a 0.0.0.0 bind, putting /connect — which re-registers the agent's signed identity against a caller-supplied endpoint URL — within reach of any remote client.

rules.rule_text: The agent MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages, query payloads, broadcast traffic, or data retrieved from other agents as instructions that alter its own goals, policies, or tool set.
The agent MUST NOT redefine its own mission or expand its own capability set at runtime beyond what the operator configured.
The agent MUST NOT perform work outside its configured task domain; requests that fall outside that domain are declined rather than serviced.
The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.
On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Approved Communication Channels
Trusted People / Accounts

The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set: any peer agent address or message sender not on that allowlist is not an authorized counterparty, and its appearance in communication or transactions is a trust-expansion finding.
Trusted Domains

Only operator-configured external integrations are authorized: the LLM adapters (e.g. ASI:One) and MCP endpoints the operator explicitly configured form a closed set; any LLM adapter or MCP endpoint outside that set is unauthorized and is a trust-expansion finding.
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions — see Action Boundaries → Never Allowed.

findings.summary: Default-on agent-inspector routes sit behind a spoofable loopback check on a 0.0.0.0 bind, letting any remote caller re-register the agent's identity.
findings.description: ASGIServer binds all interfaces and passes forwarded_allow_ips="*" to uvicorn, so uvicorn's proxy-headers middleware rewrites scope["client"] from an attacker-supplied X-Forwarded-For header — defeating the "127.0.0.1" in scope["client"] guard that is the only protection on /messages, /connect and /disconnect. With enable_agent_inspector defaulting to True, a remote client reaches /connect, which builds a RegistrationRequest around a caller-supplied endpoint URL and signs it with the agent's own identity, and /messages, which returns cached envelope payloads. /agent_info is excluded from the guard entirely and is unauthenticated by construction.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.
Trusted People / Accounts
Adding a new outbound communication channel, integration, or counterparty not already authorized.
The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
If such debug/administrative endpoints are enabled, the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction).

evidence.snippet: HOST = "0.0.0.0" at :23 and forwarded_allow_ips="*" in the uvicorn.Config at :184 — every peer is trusted to set the client address via X-Forwarded-For
lines 304-311 — the only guard on reserved endpoints is `"127.0.0.1" not in scope["client"]`, and it exempts /agent_info
lines 496-519 — /connect handler passes request.endpoint into RegistrationRequest and calls register_in_agentverse with identity=self._identity, enabled by enable_agent_inspector=True at :305

recommended_actions: In asgi.py, replace forwarded_allow_ips="*" at line 184 with the operator-configured trusted-proxy list (uvicorn's 127.0.0.1 default when unset), and make HOST at line 23 a constructor parameter defaulting to 127.0.0.1.

Flip enable_agent_inspector at agent.py:305 to default False, and require an operator-supplied bearer token on /connect, /disconnect, /messages and /agent_info rather than relying on a network-position check.

findings.summary: The shipped Helm chart carries a working default agent seed in values.yaml, deriving a publicly-known identity and wallet for any chart-default deployment.
findings.description: agent.seed is a committed literal phrase in the chart's default values, and the secrets template base64-encodes it straight into a Kubernetes Secret as UAGENT_SEED. Identity.from_seed and derive_key_from_seed turn that phrase deterministically into both the agent's signing key and its ledger wallet key, so anyone reading the public repository can reproduce the identity and drain or impersonate any agent deployed on chart defaults.
policy_rule_text: Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.

evidence.snippet: agent.seed is set to a committed literal phrase (value not reproduced) rather than left empty or required
UAGENT_SEED is rendered as `.Values.agent.seed | b64enc`, so the chart default becomes the deployed agent's seed with no override required

recommended_actions: Remove the literal from values.yaml:16, leave agent.seed empty, and make the chart fail rendering when it is unset (required in secrets.yaml) so a seed must be supplied per deployment.
Treat the committed phrase as compromised: rotate any agent identity or wallet ever deployed from chart defaults, and document seed provisioning in deployment/README.md.

findings.summary: The runtime authenticates senders but never authorizes them — the counterparty allowlist is an opt-in protocol that defaults to allow-all.
findings.description: Envelope signatures are verified, but no code path asks whether a verified sender is an authorized counterparty; every registered handler runs for any agent on the open network that knows the address. AccessControlList exists only inside QuotaProtocol, which an operator must adopt explicitly, and its fallback is AccessControlList(default=True) — allow everyone. Handlers registered with allow_unverified, including every on_query handler, additionally run for anonymous user-prefix senders with no privilege distinction between reading and state-changing work.
policy_rule_text: The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set: any peer agent address or message sender not on that allowlist is not an authorized counterparty, and its appearance in communication or transactions is a trust-expansion finding.
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.

evidence.snippet: lines 181-195 — `acl = acl or self.default_acl`, then `if acl is None: acl = AccessControlList(default=True)`; the whole mechanism is reachable only via QuotaProtocol, not Agent.on_message
lines 1455-1491 — handler lookup keys on schema_digest alone; the only sender test is is_user_address(), and no allowlist is consulted before _handle_message runs

recommended_actions: Add an agent-level counterparty allowlist checked in _process_single_message() before handler dispatch, so authorization is enforced on the default Agent.on_message path rather than only inside QuotaProtocol.

Change the QuotaProtocol.wrap() fallback at quota.py:183 from AccessControlList(default=True) to deny-by-default, and require handlers marked allow_unverified to declare that they perform no state-changing action.

findings.summary: Envelope expires and nonce fields are covered by the signature but never checked on receipt, so any captured message replays indefinitely.
findings.description: Envelope._digest folds expires and nonce into the signed digest, giving the protocol the raw material for freshness and anti-replay, but the receive path in asgi.py verifies the signature and dispatches without comparing expires to the current time or tracking nonces. The outbound builder compounds this by never populating nonce at all, so every envelope the runtime emits is replayable verbatim by anyone who observes it — including an intermediary at a plaintext peer endpoint.
policy_rule_text: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions — see Action Boundaries → Never Allowed.

evidence.snippet: lines 363-391 — env.verify() then dispatch_msg(); env.expires is read only at :390 to size the sync-response wait, and no nonce or replay cache is consulted
lines 509-519 — the outbound Envelope is constructed with version, sender, target, session, schema_digest, protocol_digest and expires, but no nonce, before env.sign()

recommended_actions: In asgi.py, reject the envelope before dispatch when env.expires is absent or already past, mirroring the freshness the digest already commits to.
Populate nonce in context.py:509 and keep a bounded per-sender seen-nonce set in the agent's storage so a replayed envelope is dropped rather than re-handled.

findings.summary: Synchronous response envelopes are built without a signature, and the requesting agent skips verification entirely when a signature is absent.
findings.description: enclose_response_raw assembles the response envelope and returns it without ever calling env.sign(), so every synchronous reply the ASGI server produces is unauthenticated. On the requesting side send_exchange_envelope only verifies when a signature happens to be present, so an unsigned response is accepted and handed to dispatch_sync_response_envelope. Any party able to answer at a resolved endpoint can therefore forge a reply that the requesting agent treats as coming from the intended peer.

evidence.snippet: lines 404-432 — enclose_response_raw builds the response Envelope, calls encode_payload, and returns model_dump_json() with no sign() step
`if env.signature:` at :157 makes verification conditional on the responder having chosen to sign, so an omitted signature bypasses the check rather than failing it

recommended_actions: Sign the response envelope in enclose_response_raw() with the responding agent's identity before it is returned by the /submit sync path in asgi.py.
Change communication.py:157 to require a signature on any response whose sender is an agent address, rejecting unsigned responses instead of accepting them.

findings.summary: No approval gate, threshold or authorization flag exists on any wallet-spending path, and Almanac registration spends funds automatically at startup.
findings.description: The remit puts on-chain value transfer out of scope by default and requires human approval above a configured threshold, but the runtime has no such parameter, no gate and no halt condition anywhere. AlmanacContract.register attaches the registration fee as transaction funds and broadcasts with the agent's wallet as part of ordinary startup, with retries, and no operator authorization is consulted at any point.
policy_rule_text: On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
Any on-chain value transfer or spend of wallet funds above the operator-configured value-transfer approval threshold parameter (`value_transfer_approval_threshold`).
On-chain value transfers are out of scope by default: the agent MUST NOT perform any on-chain value transfer or spend wallet funds unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers.
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.

evidence.snippet: lines 512-545 — `fee = self.get_registration_fee(...)`, `funds = f"{fee}{denom}"`, then prepare_and_broadcast_basic_transaction in a retry loop, reached from the default registration policy at agent startup
lines 429-436 — DefaultRegistrationPolicy is constructed with the agent's ledger and wallet whenever no policy is supplied; no approval threshold parameter exists on Agent.__init__

recommended_actions: Add a value_transfer_approval_threshold parameter to Agent.__init__ and interpose a policy check in network.py before any transaction carrying funds is broadcast, halting and logging when the amount exceeds it or authorization is absent.
Make paid Almanac registration opt-in — when no authorization flag is set, register through the fee-free Agentverse API path and surface the skipped on-chain registration to the operator.

findings.summary: Identity and wallet private keys are auto-generated into a plaintext JSON file in the working directory with default permissions and no guard.
findings.description: When an agent is constructed with a name but no seed, get_or_create_private_keys writes both the identity signing key and the ledger wallet key as hex strings into private_keys.json in the process working directory. The write uses a plain open() with no chmod, umask tightening or encryption anywhere in either package, so the file lands world- or group-readable under a typical umask. This is also where the remit's halt-and-alert-on-key-material obligation should bite: key material crosses out of process memory with no interposition, redaction or operator notification.
policy_rule_text: Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.
Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.

evidence.snippet: lines 113-127 — save_private_keys writes {"identity_key": ..., "wallet_key": ...} via json.dump to private_keys.json in os.getcwd() with no permission handling
lines 130-150 — get_or_create_private_keys is invoked from Agent._initialize_wallet_and_identity whenever seed is None and name is set, so the plaintext file is created silently on first run

recommended_actions: Create private_keys.json with 0o600 (open with os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_WRONLY, 0o600)) in save_private_keys(), and fail loudly if an existing file is group- or world-readable.
Emit an explicit warning from _initialize_wallet_and_identity() when keys are auto-persisted to disk, and document the seed-from-environment path as the supported production configuration.

findings.summary: get_or_create_private_keys persists a freshly generated wallet key that is not the one it returns, so the running wallet's key is never saved.
findings.description: The function generates a wallet key, then calls save_private_keys with a second, independently generated PrivateKey() while returning the first. The agent therefore runs on a wallet whose private key exists only in process memory, while private_keys.json records a different key for a wallet address that is never used. Any funds sent to the running agent's wallet — including registration-fee balance — become permanently unrecoverable at restart, and the agent silently comes back up under a different ledger address.

evidence.snippet: lines 147-150 — `wallet_key = PrivateKey().private_key` then `save_private_keys(name, identity_key, PrivateKey().private_key)` then `return identity_key, wallet_key`; the saved and returned wallet keys are different objects
lines 590-592 — the returned wallet_key becomes LocalWallet(PrivateKey(wallet_key)), binding the live agent to the key that was never written to disk

recommended_actions: In storage/__init__.py:149, pass the already-generated wallet_key to save_private_keys() instead of calling PrivateKey() a second time.
Add a regression test asserting that two successive get_or_create_private_keys(name) calls return the same wallet key and that it matches the persisted file.

findings.summary: The default inbound message path has no rate limit, queue bound or concurrency ceiling on a publicly-bound server.
findings.description: QuotaProtocol documents itself as "Default: Not rate limited", and the base Agent.on_message path it would wrap is not used by default, so an agent bound to 0.0.0.0 accepts envelopes at whatever rate a sender offers. The internal message queue is an unbounded asyncio.Queue, and with handle_messages_concurrently enabled each message spawns an unbounded handler task, so a single sender can drive memory and task growth without tripping any ceiling.

evidence.snippet: module docstring at :9 — "Default: Not rate limited, but you can set a default during initialization"; the mechanism only applies to handlers registered through QuotaProtocol
`self._message_queue = asyncio.Queue()` at :410 is unbounded, and _process_single_message at :1471-1491 creates an unbounded handler task per message when _handle_messages_concurrently is set

recommended_actions: Give asyncio.Queue() at agent.py:410 a bounded maxsize and shed or 429 inbound envelopes when it is full, rather than buffering without limit.
Apply a conservative default RateLimit per sender on the base Agent.on_message path so rate limiting is inherited rather than requiring adoption of QuotaProtocol.

findings.summary: The published package floor-pins two dependencies with no upper bound, and no dependency or security scanning runs in CI.
findings.description: uagents declares uagents-core and cosmpy with open-ended >= constraints while its other dependencies are properly capped, so a downstream install resolves whatever major version those two projects publish next — including the package that supplies the agent's own identity and signing code. The committed lockfiles protect only development checkouts, not consumers, and neither the CI workflows nor the pre-commit configuration runs a vulnerability scanner, SBOM step or dependency-update bot.

evidence.snippet: lines 15-21 — `"uagents-core (>=0.4.8)"` and `"cosmpy (>=0.12.1)"` carry no upper bound, while pydantic, uvicorn and aiohttp are all range-capped
hooks are ruff and pyupgrade only; the four .github/workflows files contain no bandit, codeql, semgrep, pip-audit or dependabot configuration

recommended_actions: Cap uagents-core and cosmpy with major-version upper bounds in python/pyproject.toml so a breaking or hostile release of the identity/ledger layer cannot be pulled into a downstream install.
Add a dependency-audit job (pip-audit or equivalent) and a dependency-update bot to .github/workflows, and publish an SBOM alongside the release artifacts.

findings.summary: Signed envelopes are POSTed to whatever URL the registry returns, with no scheme, host or TLS validation on the outbound destination.
findings.description: The resolver hands endpoint URLs straight from the Almanac API or contract record to send_exchange_envelope, which POSTs to them unconditionally — so a peer that registers a plaintext, loopback or link-local endpoint receives the agent's traffic at that address. Because ctx.broadcast discovers recipients from the Almanac search API rather than from an operator list, the destination set is not fully operator-chosen, which turns a registry entry into a way to steer an agent's outbound requests. The Agentverse base URL itself can likewise be downgraded to plaintext http through the agentverse config parser.
policy_rule_text: Approved Communication Channels
Trusted Domains

evidence.snippet: lines 145-152 — `for endpoint in endpoints: ... session.post(endpoint, headers=headers, data=envelope.model_dump_json())` with no scheme allowlist, host filter or TLS requirement on the resolver-supplied URL
lines 120-132 — parse_agentverse_config accepts a caller-supplied protocol of "http", and http_prefix falls back through protocol_override before defaulting to https

recommended_actions: Validate resolver output in communication.py before dispatch: require https (with an explicit opt-in for local development) and reject loopback, link-local and private-range hosts unless the operator allowlists them.
Restrict the protocol override in config.py:128 to development configurations so a production agent cannot be pointed at a plaintext Agentverse base URL.

findings.summary: Message handling produces no action-level audit record, and repeated signature-verification failures are logged individually with no alerting.
findings.description: _process_single_message dispatches a verified envelope to its handler without emitting any log line — only unrecognized digests, parse failures and handler exceptions are recorded — so a successful inbound action leaves no trace in the log stream at all. Logging itself is free-form text with no schema, which blocks automated detection rules, and a failed envelope verification produces a single warning with no counter or threshold, so the remit's "alert on repeated failures" condition has nothing to fire on. The one structured, durable record of envelopes, EnvelopeHistory backed by storage, is off unless store_message_history is explicitly enabled.
policy_rule_text: Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.
Routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs.

evidence.snippet: lines 1471-1491 — handler dispatch emits no log record; the only logging on this path is the unrecognized-digest warning at :1374 and the exception handlers in _handle_message at :1364-1371
lines 6-9 — a single free-form Formatter ("%(asctime)s,%(msecs)03d %(name)s %(levelname)s %(message)s") with no structured or JSON output option

recommended_actions: Emit a structured record (sender, schema digest, session, handler, outcome) from _process_single_message() for every dispatched message, and offer a JSON formatter alongside the text one in uagents_core/logger.py.
Track verification failures per sender in asgi.py and raise a distinct warning once a threshold is crossed, so repeated unverified senders surface as one alertable event rather than n isolated lines.

positives.title: ECDSA envelope signature verification on every agent-to-agent message
positives.description: Inbound envelopes from agent-prefixed senders are cryptographically verified against the sender's address before dispatch, and a verification failure rejects the request with a 400 rather than falling through.

positives.title: No code-execution surface anywhere in the runtime
positives.description: Neither package contains subprocess, os.system, eval, exec, pickle or dynamic-import calls, so the remit's forbidden-tool clause is satisfied structurally rather than by policy.

positives.title: Typed schema validation on every inbound message and REST payload
positives.description: Envelopes are validated against the Envelope model, payloads parsed into a registered pydantic Model, and unrecognized schema digests dropped before any handler runs.

positives.title: Unverified message handling is opt-in, not the default
positives.description: on_message registers handlers in the signed map unless allow_unverified is explicitly set True, and a signed handler actively refuses a user-prefix sender with an error reply.

positives.title: Rate-limiting and access-control primitives ship with the framework
positives.description: QuotaProtocol provides per-sender sliding-window rate limits and an AccessControlList with allow, block and bypass sets, giving operators a first-party path to the remit's counterparty allowlist.

positives.title: Private-key file is excluded from version control
positives.description: The repository-root .gitignore excludes *.json, which covers the private_keys.json and <name>_data.json files the runtime writes into the working directory.

positives.title: Dependency lockfiles are committed for all packages
positives.description: uv.lock and uagents-core/poetry.lock pin the full resolved dependency graph for reproducible builds, even though the published manifests use ranges.

rows.purpose: Component log lines from uagents-core modules (identity, registration, protocol); captures errors and status messages, not agent actions
Agent working state; also holds full envelope payloads per session when store_message_history is enabled, and QuotaProtocol per-sender request counters

raise_posture.weighted_rationale: Ad hoc. The runtime has one genuinely strong axis — cryptographic message authentication and typed schema dispatch, with no execution surface at all — and that carries its domain confinement. Everything built on top of that authentication is thin: authorization, replay defence, approval gating on wallet spend, and key-material protection are either absent or shipped off by default, and supply-chain, adversarial-testing and monitoring practice are ad hoc across the board. The result is a framework that reliably tells a deployed agent who is talking to it, and then leaves every decision about what that party may cause to happen to the application author.

categories.name: Limit Your Domain
categories.rationale: Domain is confined in code rather than prose — _process_single_message() in agent.py drops any envelope whose schema digest is not in the agent's registered model set, handlers are fixed at construction, and a grep of both packages finds no subprocess, eval, exec or deserialization surface to escape into.

categories.name: Balance Your Knowledge Base
categories.rationale: Inbound data sources are tightly scoped and strongly typed, but counterparty-supplied payloads are written verbatim into EnvelopeHistory and, with store_message_history enabled, into the same plaintext KeyValueStore JSON file that holds the agent's own state, and are served back out of the default-on /messages route.

categories.name: Implement Zero Trust
categories.rationale: Authentication is real and operative — ECDSA envelope verification in asgi.py, typed validation, and signed handlers that refuse unverified user-prefix senders — but authorization is absent by default, replay and expiry are never enforced, sync response envelopes are neither signed nor required to be, and no approval gate exists on any wallet-spending path.

categories.name: Manage Your Supply Chain
categories.rationale: Lockfiles are committed and most dependencies are range-capped, but the published uagents manifest floor-pins uagents-core and cosmpy with no upper bound, no SBOM or dependency-vulnerability scanning runs in CI, and the shipped Helm chart carries a working default agent seed.

categories.name: Build an AI Red Team
categories.rationale: Fifteen test modules exercise functional paths and a documented disclosure process exists in SECURITY.md, but the suite contains no adversarial case at all — test_msg_verify.py asserts only that a valid signature verifies, with no tampered-signature, replay, or malformed-envelope test, and CI runs no security scanner.

categories.name: Monitor Continuously
categories.rationale: Logging is free-form text through get_logger() in uagents_core/logger.py with no schema and no action-level record of inbound message handling, and the one structured, durable envelope record — EnvelopeHistory with store_message_history — is off by default.
